prerequisites: A2 English level for university access exams (PAU)
B2 English level (CEFR) for optimal use of English language activities

learning_outcomes.text: Read, draft and prepare documentation in English on a scientific-technical topic in the field of study.
Associate technical specifications with transmission and reception topologies as well as the different subsystems that compose them.
Identify non-ideal behaviors of components based on operating frequency.
Manage the physical parameters of each subsystem, associating its behavior with the complete system.
Build a complete system from different subsystems.
Select the most suitable technology and components for each application in different frequency bands.

syllabus_topics: General transmission and reception schemes for radio systems
Specifications and selection criteria based on application
Behavior of components in radiofrequency and microwave bands
Selection of components based on frequency band
Filters: Types and general characteristics of filters. Specifications as a subsystem and selection criteria
Mixers: Types and general characteristics of mixers. Specifications as a subsystem and selection criteria
Amplifiers: Types and general characteristics of amplifiers. Specifications as a subsystem and selection criteria
Oscillators: Types and general characteristics of oscillators. Specifications as a subsystem and selection criteria
Selection of manufacturing technology based on operating band

assessment_methods.method: Two tests during classroom practices (individual questions and oral presentation in English)
Written face-to-face exam (theoretical, theoretical-practical questions, and/or problems)
Assessment of laboratory practices (reports or in-situ evaluation)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.2 * (T1) + 0.6 * (T2) + 0.2 * (P1). A minimum weighted score of 5 points is required to pass the course. Students are considered 'No Presentado' if participation in evaluation activities is less than 50% of the total grade; otherwise, unpresented activities are graded with 0. In the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of a written exam (T2 type), and practical content evaluation can optionally be replaced by the ordinary call's practical grade. The extraordinary grade is (0.8 * theoretical content) + (0.2 * practical content).
